what_it_predicts: P(exactly one offer), given that the solicitation ends in a competed award with a usable offer count. A risk indicator about the market for a requirement, not a statement about anyone's conduct.
outcome_rule: Earliest base action (purchase order, definitive contract or contract vehicle) with the same normalised solicitation number, dated on or after first posting and at most 730 days later. Resolved only if competed (A, D, E, F, CDO) with 1 to 998 offers. Numbers shorter than 8 characters are not matched.

data.funnel_note: Sector here is the sector known on the posting day; 'unknown' means SAM.gov gave no agency and the number matched no earlier award.

no_leakage: Only the first version of the notice and awards from quarters ending at least 1 full quarter(s) before the posting quarter (a 12-quarter window). Not used: amendments, final deadline, award notices.

shipped.name_in_evaluation: logistic v2, half-life 3 years, correction by sector
shipped.training_window: all earlier years, time-decay weights with a half-life of 3 years
why: Rule 1 (fixed before the candidates were fitted): 12 logistic candidates (6 raw models, each with one correction for all sectors or a correction by sector), scored by log loss pooled over the last five test years, FY2022 to FY2026. A simpler candidate gives way only to one that lowers that log loss by at least 0.5%.

The lowest log loss is 0.4837 (logistic v2, half-life 3 years, correction by sector). The model shipped until now (one correction for all sectors) has 0.4920. Rule 1 selects logistic v2, half-life 3 years, with 0.4861 (-1.2% against the model shipped until now; lower in 5 of the 5 years). It is the candidate with the fewest changes within 0.5% of the lowest log loss.

Amendment, made after seeing the results (November 10, 2026). Rule 1 selected R2 + P (time decay with a half-life of 3 years, one correction for all sectors). R2 + S (the same model with the correction by sector) is shipped instead. This choice was made after the results were known, so it overrides the rule written down before fitting.

Reason: the revision was made because the forecasts were miscalibrated by sector. Rule 1 measured only pooled log loss, where the correction by sector falls 0.01 points short of the 0.5% margin (0.49%), but it largely removes the problem the revision was for.

Calibration slopes in test years 2024 to 2026 (1.00 is ideal): civilian except GSA 0.74 to 0.86 with R2 + P, 0.96 to 1.09 with R2 + S; Defense 1.26 to 1.38 with R2 + P, 1.11 to 1.23 with R2 + S. The public scores are reported by sector, so a known miscalibration by sector should not be shipped.
Log loss of the shipped model, pooled over FY2022 to FY2026: 0.4837 (-1.7% against the model shipped until now).

The correction is fitted by sector group: Defense, and civilian (civilian agencies except GSA together with GSA, which has about 150 resolved solicitations a year). A solicitation whose sector is unknown on the posting day gets the one correction fitted on all sectors.

Gradient boosting against the shipped logistic regression, pooled over all test years: log loss 0.4876 against 0.4897 (+0.4%), better in 61% of the test years, calibration slope 1.00 against 0.98. That is not clearly better by the fixed rule (2% lower log loss, 80% of the years, slope no worse), so the readable logistic regression is shipped.

calibration.other_sectors: a solicitation whose sector is unknown on the posting day uses a_pooled and b_pooled

selection.rule: Rule 1 in the docstring of scripts/30_model_v2.py, written down before the candidates were fitted. Score: log loss pooled over the last five test years. Outcomes exist only for solicitations that ended in a competed award with a usable offer count.
The newest test year (FY2026) is incomplete: Defense awards are published 90 days late, and slow awards are still missing.
The corrections are fitted on the held-out predictions of three test years.

evaluation.design: Rolling origin. Train: posted before fiscal year t and awarded before fiscal year t. Test: posted in fiscal year t. Calibrated rows use a correction fitted on earlier held-out years only (one for all sectors, or by sector group for the rows named 'correction by sector'). Each evaluation fit uses a seeded random sample of at most 200,000 training rows; the final model uses every row.

scoring.history_in_model_file: the last 20 quarters; refresh with history_from_awards and merge_history

calculator.what: Aggregates for the explorer's what-if calculator: the model's full-precision coefficients, and typical values (medians of the training rows) for the inputs that come from history. Office history is replaced by the median of the sector, so the calculator shows a typical buying office of the sector, not any real one.
calculator.component_note: Component (sub-agency) effects are part of the model but are not published. Each agency gets one typical component effect (the median over its recent solicitations) and the number of component levels the model has for it.

crosswalk_sam_to_usaspending.note: SAM.gov department and sub-tier names mapped to USAspending agencies. Kept in the private model file only, because it names components below agency level.

components: Component (sub-agency) effects are part of the model but are not published.
private_files: The model file, the training table and the history tables hold office-level history and stay in the private data folder. This card, the coefficient table and the evaluation tables are at agency level or coarser.
caveats: Conditional forecast: it says nothing about whether a solicitation leads to an award, or to a competed one.
Only solicitations whose number appears on a USAspending award can be scored. Civilian awards often lack the number.
Before fiscal year 2020 about half of the archived notices carry no agency or office; the agency is then taken from earlier awards with the same number start.
Market depth is one 2026 snapshot of SAM.gov registrations applied to every year. It is not an outcome, but it is not historical either.
Defense data are published 90 days late; the two-quarter lag covers that.

Single-offer outcomes became more predictable in recent years, mostly in Defense. A model fitted on many years and a correction fitted on three years lag behind such a drift; the out-of-time tables show how much.

On the held-out years behind the correction (FY2024 to FY2026), Defense forecasts above 0.7 averaged 0.75 and came true 0.69 of the time (4,270 solicitations). So the highest Defense forecasts run high.
The shipped Defense correction (slope 1.45) is steeper than any used in the out-of-time evaluation (at most 1.34). So the published scores do not fully cover it.
Award years present when this card was built: 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026. Rerun all three steps when more arrive.
